title: Everything slid right because the seeker feed handed device pixels to setViewport, which takes CSS pixels: on a Retina surface the glass showed the bottom-left quarter of the frame blown up
context: Owner, Safari on macOS, build f1fd12b1: 'Gunship still has miscalibrated hud vs where it shoots. Tank still appears on the right of the screen instead of center. Everything off to the right.' Headless Chrome measured zero offset at dpr 1 and 2 (2026-09-23-seat-changes-robust), so the seat work was the wrong layer. It was also the wrong INSTRUMENT: seatState() reports the camera's own projection, and a GL viewport fault never touches a projection matrix, so every assertion the suites owned was blind to this by construction.
outcome: src/fx/story-monitor.js scissors the seeker feed into a corner of the main canvas and then puts the main viewport back. three's setViewport/setScissor take CSS pixels — WebGLRenderer multiplies them by its own pixel ratio on the way to gl.viewport, which is exactly what setSize(w,h) relies on when it calls setViewport(0,0,w,h). The monitor passed DEVICE pixels to all four calls, so every frame it drew left the main viewport dpr times too large, anchored at the drawing buffer's bottom-left corner. At dpr 1 that is an identity and nothing shows; at dpr 2 the visible canvas then displays the bottom-left quarter of the frame at 2x, so the whole world slides right and up while the DOM overlays (the gunship reticle SVG, the tank's place on the glass) stay where they were — the owner's three symptoms at once, in every view, from one line. Fixed by keeping CSS pixels for setViewport/setScissor and device pixels only for the feed's drawImage, which reads the backing store (src/fx/story-monitor.js:29-34). laser-scope.js was checked and is already correct: it takes its numbers from renderer.getSize(), which is CSS pixels. Regression: a new --gunship step 'gunship-retina' loads the seat at deviceScaleFactor 2 and asserts gl.getParameter(gl.VIEWPORT) still covers the whole drawing buffer; go() grew a dpr argument because the renderer reads devicePixelRatio once, when it is built, so a ratio applied after the load never reaches it. Reproduced BEFORE at [0,0,5760,3600] against a 2880x1800 buffer, PASS after. Safari could not confirm the dpr-2 case on kainode: its only display is 3440x1440 at dpr 1, where the fault is a no-op, and safaridriver is refused ('Allow Remote Automation' is GUI- and password-gated, and the Safari preferences container is TCC-protected). Real Safari 26.6.2 was driven instead through a new harness that needs no WebDriver — artifacts/qa/safari-probe-server.mjs serves the repository and injects artifacts/qa/probe.js on ?probe=1, and the page POSTs its own measurements back — and it measured the surface exactly right there before and after the change (dpr 1, canvas 1639x1102 attr and CSS, gl viewport [0,0,1639,1102], tank NDC x 0.00000, reticle-vs-aim 0.00 px). The owner's Retina confirmation is still outstanding.
alternatives: Chasing the seat/camera logic again: rejected, seatState() reads the projection and the projection was already exact in both browsers.
A Safari-specific branch on the user agent: rejected, the fault is a units bug that is wrong in every browser and merely invisible at dpr 1.
Re-applying renderer.setPixelRatio on resize so a display change reaches the renderer: real but separate, and not needed for this bug; left alone.
evidence: scripts/browser-test.mjs --gunship, step gunship-retina: before the fix, AssertionError gl VIEWPORT [0,0,5760,3600] vs drawingBuffer [2880,1800]; after, PASS gunship-retina.
Chrome green after the change: --seats, --gunship, --phone, --defense; npm test (121 test programs) and npm run check.

Safari 26.6.2 (Version/26.6.2, dpr 1) via artifacts/qa/safari-probe-server.mjs + artifacts/qa/probe.js: third-surface attr [1639,1102] css [1639,1102] glViewport [0,0,1639,1102]; third-seat tank [0,-0.41404]; gunship-reticle dx 0.00 dy 0.00 — the same numbers before and after, as expected where the fault is an identity.
vendor/three.module.js:28839 — setSize(width,height) calls setViewport(0,0,width,height) with CSS pixels, which fixes the unit.
src/fx/laser-scope.js:76-91 — the other scissored view, correct, and the contrast that named the bug.
